evals.prompt: my llama-server only does like 8 tok/s on an RTX 4070 with a 13B Q4_K_M model and the GPU looks basically idle. help me figure out what's wrong and fix it.
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses partial/absent GPU offload as the primary cause, checks the backend and -ngl/served layer log, and gives concrete fixes (raise -ngl, reduce -c, enable -fa + q8_0 KV, or drop quant) plus a way to verify with llama-bench.
expectations: Asks for or determines the backend/build (CUDA vs CPU-only) before recommending flags
Identifies missing or partial GPU offload (-ngl) as the likely cause
Recommends verifying via the llama.cpp startup log 'offloaded X/Y layers' and/or llama-bench baseline
Gives an actual corrective launch command with -ngl and -fa included

evals.prompt: I want to find the best context size and KV cache type for my 8B Q4_K_M model on a 24GB 4090. Set me up a benchmark I can actually run.
evals.expected_output: Sets up a reproducible llama-bench sweep over -c and matched KV cache types, reminds that KV types must match, and produces a launch command from the winner.
expectations: Uses llama-bench (not guesses) to compare configurations
Keeps KV cache key and value types matched (never mixes q8_0 with q4_0)
Captures a baseline and repeats runs rather than trusting a single measurement
Ends with a concrete llama-server launch command

evals.prompt: we're serving a Qwen2.5-14B Q5_K_M on one 24GB GPU via llama-server for a small team (~4 people using it at once). How should I configure --parallel and context, and how do I know if it's actually coping?
evals.expected_output: Explains --parallel slot allocation and that --ctx-size is total across slots (so per-slot = ctx/parallel), suggests a reference config, and describes checking the /metrics queue-depth and slot utilization to know when to add slots or switch to vLLM.
expectations: Explains that --ctx-size is the total across all slots, not per slot
Recommends a --parallel value matched to the ~4 concurrent users
Mentions monitoring via --metrics (queue depth / slot utilization) or equivalent
Notes the ~5-10 concurrent user threshold where vLLM becomes the better choice
